source: Sample_Documents/fdic-ar-1956.pdf page 36 (FDIC Annual Report 1956, Exhibit 1, balance sheet at June 30, 1956)
labeling: Hand-labeled by reading the 300 DPI render. THE LABELS ARE CHECKED BY THE PAGE'S OWN ARITHMETIC: seven sums, all exact to the dollar, and the sheet balances -- total assets equal total liabilities plus the deposit insurance fund. A misread digit in any figure that appears in a sum breaks that sum, so this ground truth is verified rather than merely careful. Money is labeled WITHOUT the dollar sign: on this page the $ sits at the column edge as a marker rather than against the number, and score.py strips currency signs before comparing anyway.

reconciliation.note: Seven sums the page asserts about itself, every one exact to the dollar. reconcile.py evaluates them against the hand labels FIRST and refuses to grade a parser if one fails -- a mistyped label would otherwise show up as every parser breaking the same sum, which reads exactly like a finding. Subtraction is written as addition, because the checker sums its terms: the net receivership figure plus the loss estimate equals the gross.

not_labeled: The auditor's opinion paragraph and the table caption above the exhibit are prose, not tabular data, and are left out so the score is not diluted by ordinary body text that every parser reads. The two inline figures inside the securities label ARE labeled -- face_value and market_value -- because a parser that lifts them as if they were column values is making exactly the mistake this corpus exists to catch.
